name: Hypertrophy Specific Training

lead: Hypertrophy Specific Training (HST) is a lifting method aimed at increasing muscle size, which is the main way lifters improve their physique. It trains each muscle several times a week and raises the load across a cycle.
It was popularised after an October 2000 ThinkMuscle newsletter article by writer Bryan Haycock, and its fan base spread through bodybuilding forums.

paras: The method rests on four principles: frequency, mechanical load, progression and strategic deconditioning. A commonly described cycle moves from sets of 15 to 10 to 5 over weeks, then a planned break, with only one or two sets per exercise per session.
As a resistance-training plan it carries ordinary lifting injury risks, which rise with heavy loads and poor technique. Planned breaks are part of the design.

angle.text: HST is a programme for adding muscle, which changes physique directly. Lifters follow its cycles to organise frequency, loading and rest.

lead: Hypertrophy Specific Training, or HST, is a resistance-training method focused on muscle growth. It was popularised following an October 2000 ThinkMuscle newsletter article by Bryan Haycock [1].

Lifters use it to build more muscle, which is a direct route to a larger, more defined physique. Its four major principles are frequency, mechanical load, progression and strategic deconditioning [1].

Proponents say muscles should be stimulated several times a week rather than hit hard once and left for a week, that load is the key driver of growth, and that after the heaviest loads a pause lets muscles become responsive again [1]. The programme's details come from its own authors and fan sites and have not been validated by independent trials [1].
infobox: Frequency, mechanical load, progression, strategic deconditioning

paras: Frequency: train each muscle several times a week [1]. Progressive load: weight is increased across the cycle; one description has 15s in weeks one and two, 10s in weeks three and four, 5s in weeks five and six, then negatives, more 5s or drops, with deconditioning at weeks nine and ten [1]. Strategic deconditioning: a stop in training after heavy loading so the muscle can respond again; suggested lengths vary [1]. Volume is kept to one or two sets per exercise per workout [1].
No independent scientific validation of the programme as a whole was found; the cycle lengths are the programme's own recommendations [1].
